meta.title: FRAME ZERO · AI Video Hackathon
meta.description: FRAME ZERO is an AI video hackathon touring China. Teams of 2–6 get eight hours and a video API to make an original one-minute film.

concept.label: FRAME ZERO · About
concept.heading: Why “Frame Zero”?
body: Every film has a first frame. Before it there is an earlier moment: no script yet, no character names, the camera still off — just an idea that has started to take shape.
Many ideas stop there, because the equipment isn’t good enough, the team isn’t there yet, there isn’t time, or we don’t feel ready.
concept.calloutTitle: FRAME ZERO gives that idea eight hours.
concept.calloutBody: A team, a room to work in and a video API — enough to turn the story in your head into a film people can watch.

points.text: per edition, in teams of 2–6, free of charge

format.label: Format · Judging · Prizes
format.heading: Eight hours from script to final cut
format.sub: No experience needed: participants get online tutorials for the video API before the event, plus training and Q&A in the team chat.

rules.title: Made on site
rules.body: From 10:00 to 18:00, teams write, storyboard, generate and edit in the same room.

rules.title: Teams of 2–6
rules.body: Some people write, some think in pictures, some want to dig into the video API — a team puts them together.

rules.title: One video API
rules.body: Footage must be generated with the video API provided. Teams handle script, storyboard and edit themselves and may use AI along the way.

rules.title: Submit a film
rules.body: At 18:00 each team exports and submits an original film of about one minute.

schedule.detail: Form teams, learn how to call the video API and test a first shot. Agree on a theme and roles, then start writing.
Break the script into shots — what each shows, how long it runs, how it cuts to the next. Settle characters and look, write prompts and start generating footage.
Pick the best shots, fill the gaps and start editing: order, transitions, sound and subtitles. Generating and editing run in parallel until the film comes together.
Submissions close. Everyone watches the films together and talks through what they wanted to say and the choices they made.

format.judgingHeading: Judging · winners announced on the day
format.judgingBody: Technical complexity matters less than what a film is trying to say, and whether each shot serves the story.
questions: Does the film have something to say?
Does the technology make that clearer?
Do the creators stand behind their choices?
awards: Winners chosen on site; prize money set per edition
A certificate for every team that finishes a film
Official mascot merch: stickers, badges, tote bags and more
format.studioAlt: Pixel illustration: teams of students editing video on laptops in a bright classroom

stops.label: Editions · Track record
stops.heading: From Wuhan, one edition at a time
stops.sub: The first edition ran in September 2026; FRAME ZERO now tours universities, innovation parks and other organizations.

items.name: Wuhan University
items.body: The first FRAME ZERO. Twenty-three teams worked from seven briefs, on subjects from campus life and city culture to public-interest stories. Supported by the university’s Yubing Insight team and student volunteers.

items.name: Shandong University of Technology
items.body: Hosted by the AI Lab of the School of Computer Science and Technology in Lab 508. More than 40 students and teachers took part; three judges scored each film on clarity, a memorable idea and smooth editing.

items.name: Xiamen · Egret Youth Hackathon
items.body: An AIGC video edition co-organized with Xiamen Torch OPC Innovation Community at Xiamen Software Park Phase I (North). Teams of 1–3 make a 60-second film in an open track or the park’s own brief, “Where youth stories happen”. Compute provided by AMD.

works.showreelCaption: Winners’ showreel · Wuhan University and Shandong Tech (about 2 minutes, with sound)

items.title: No More Goodbyes Under the Cherry Blossoms
Don’t Stick Today onto Tomorrow
items.team: Gao Minghuang, Zhang Jinshan, Wu Chuanshuo
items.note: A first-person monologue: the to-do list keeps growing while less and less actually gets started. All three judges voted for it.

items.title: A Stone That Stands Guard
items.team: Sun Mingyu, Ma Zihang, Yao Yican
items.note: Opens with an interview question and uses the Shigandang guardian-stone tradition to talk about people who stand up to protect their homes.

items.title: Leave the Blur to Art
items.note: An Impressionism piece that recreates the movement’s colour and feeling in AI-generated images.

items.title: Forging the Sword: Echoes of Qi
items.team: Xie Xiaobo, Han Mengyao, Gao Yining
items.note: Sets the bronze-smiths of the ancient state of Qi beside today’s creators who use code as their chisel.

items.title: Ten Flats, No Second Chances: Which One Should You Buy?
items.note: Explains the optimal stopping problem (the 37% rule) as a house-hunting decision.

items.title: The Old Bookstall
items.team: Zhang Yiping, Liu Luhui, Gao Yinuo
items.note: A boy can’t afford a rare second-hand book; the gruff stall owner quietly keeps it for him.
